requirements.statement: **Role permissions and resource limits:** Professor manages scheduling; students manage only their own jobs within their role's resource limits.
requirements.title: Recognize trusted student and Professor groups.
requirements.detail: Group memberships are static facts in rules.dl; the original bound identities do not come from agent arguments.
requirements.source: **Role permissions and resource limits:** Professor manages scheduling; students manage only their own jobs within their role's resource limits.

requirements.statement: Only Professor may approve or reject student requests, dispatch jobs, or stop another student's job.
requirements.title: Reserve approve, reject, dispatch and administrative stop for Professor.
requirements.detail: Only a Professor-bound request can match these Allow rules. Lifecycle, approval and scheduling conditions are refined in P3-P5; a failed stop confirmation commits no state change.
requirements.source: Only Professor may approve or reject student requests, dispatch jobs, or stop another student's job.

requirements.statement: PhD and Master may submit jobs and read, revise, cancel or report completion only for their own jobs.
requirements.title: Students submit within quota and operate only on their own jobs.
requirements.distilled: Guarded job tools + structured completion-report gate
requirements.detail: Submit binds the original caller as owner. Job tool guards and a Bus.send decorator enforce student ownership before effects. COMPLETION_REPORT uses the host-supplied sender and actual body.job_id; rejected reports create no delivery trace or inbox entry. This covers the app-defined structured protocol, not arbitrary free-text claims. Professor retains original finish_job access.
requirements.source: PhD and Master may submit jobs and read, revise, cancel or report completion only for their own jobs.

requirements.statement: Master may request CPU only, with at most 4 cores, 8 GB and 20 minutes of requested runtime.
requirements.title: Master uses CPU with cores <= 4, memory <= 8 GB and requested minutes <= 20.
requirements.detail: Quota is reviewed .dl configuration. The original Store still validates schemas and quotas; the policy gate adds the Datalog check before the unchanged operation.
requirements.source: Master may request CPU only, with at most 4 cores, 8 GB and 20 minutes of requested runtime.
requirements.guideNote: Original validate_spec checks positive integers.

requirements.statement: PhD may request CPU or GPU, with at most 8 cores, 32 GB and 60 minutes.
requirements.title: PhD uses CPU or GPU with cores <= 8, memory <= 32 GB and minutes <= 60.
requirements.detail: The same Datalog quota rules use the PhD group facts from .dl.
requirements.source: PhD may request CPU or GPU, with at most 8 cores, 32 GB and 60 minutes.

requirements.statement: Requests outside the owner's quota must not be admitted or dispatched; Professor cannot override these limits or physical capacity.
requirements.title: Reject over-quota admission and dispatch; require a free node with enough capacity.
requirements.detail: Requested runtime is an admission limit, not an elapsed-time watchdog. Dispatch combines WithinJobQuota and FreeCompatible in P5.
requirements.source: Requests outside the owner's quota must not be admitted or dispatched; Professor cannot override these limits or physical capacity.

requirements.statement: **Information flow and isolation:** PhD and Master keep their work private from each other, while Professor may inspect both students' work.
requirements.title: Gate single-job reads and retain original bulk/private filtering.
requirements.distilled: Datalog read gate + original output filtering
requirements.detail: Readable gates single-job reads. Original view/read_private still filter their own results. QueueViewer and PrivateReadable are currently analysis-only. Datalog can derive visible record/field IDs for a trusted result adapter to project before disclosure; that projection is not yet connected.
requirements.source: **Information flow and isolation:** PhD and Master keep their work private from each other, while Professor may inspect both students' work.
requirements.guideNote: Original view/read_private filter outputs; QueueViewer and PrivateReadable are analysis-only.

requirements.statement: Neither student may receive the other's private job specifications, inputs, results, approvals or execution receipts through tools, model contexts or messages.
requirements.title: Prevent peer disclosure across every output channel.
requirements.detail: Tool reads are scoped, but message/context IFC is incomplete. The original T2 UNSAFE_PEER_NOTE delivers private PhD data to Master outside the completion-report guard. Trusted adapters must bind actual data versions and record DependsOn before release; agents cannot supply trusted lineage. Professor mixed-private contexts also require a precision/usability decision.
requirements.source: Neither student may receive the other's private job specifications, inputs, results, approvals or execution receipts through tools, model contexts or messages.

requirements.statement: Students may send their own task details to Professor, who may inspect both students' records and share private details only with the owning student.
requirements.title: Permit owner-to-Professor sharing and owner-specific replies.
requirements.detail: No general send/receive IFC gate is installed. The P1.3 decorator checks only structured completion-report ownership; arbitrary body text and other message types remain unmediated.
requirements.source: Students may send their own task details to Professor, who may inspect both students' records and share private details only with the owning student.

requirements.statement: Forbidden and nonexistent job lookups must both return UNAVAILABLE without revealing whether a private record exists.
requirements.title: Return the same public response for a forbidden or missing job.
requirements.detail: No matching Readable means no Allow. The adapter returns the original UNAVAILABLE shape without executing the read.
requirements.source: Forbidden and nonexistent job lookups must both return UNAVAILABLE without revealing whether a private record exists.

requirements.statement: Role quotas, node specifications and aggregate busy/free availability are public; this boundary does not prevent inference from public timing or availability.
requirements.title: Keep quotas, node capacity and aggregate availability public.
requirements.detail: The original Store.view returns public capacity/availability and omits allocation tokens. No view-to-EDB mapping runs; timing inference remains outside scope.
requirements.source: Role quotas, node specifications and aggregate busy/free availability are public; this boundary does not prevent inference from public timing or availability.
requirements.guideNote: Original Store.view returns public fields and filters private collections.

requirements.statement: The authorized evaluator may inspect complete synthetic traces, but student agents must not receive that full view.
requirements.title: Restrict full evaluator traces to the evaluator.
requirements.distilled: Original convention; not a runtime guarantee
requirements.detail: The original Trace/export machinery is unchanged and not exposed by these tools. Deployment and any export endpoint must separately preserve this boundary.
requirements.source: The authorized evaluator may inspect complete synthetic traces, but student agents must not receive that full view.

requirements.statement: API credentials must never appear in agent prompts, traces or submitted files.
requirements.title: Keep credentials out of prompts, traces and submissions.
requirements.detail: No credential detector or complete secret-flow instrumentation is installed. Do not translate this obligation into a fictitious always-successful rule.
requirements.source: API credentials must never appear in agent prompts, traces or submitted files.

requirements.statement: **Evidence for job decisions:** Starting a job requires a current approval record; marking it completed requires a matching runner receipt.
requirements.title: Require recorded approval to start and recorded runner evidence to finish.
requirements.detail: P3.2 and P3.5 give the two exact joins. A natural-language agent claim creates neither record.
requirements.source: **Evidence for job decisions:** Starting a job requires a current approval record; marking it completed requires a matching runner receipt.

requirements.statement: Before dispatch, require a successful Professor approval record matching the job's current task version and exact resource request.
requirements.title: Match approval to the current job version, exact spec and policy.
requirements.detail: The original approve method returns its actual approval. The tool helper records Approval, ApprovalSpec and CurrentApproval without reading Store.snapshot.
requirements.source: Before dispatch, require a successful Professor approval record matching the job's current task version and exact resource request.
requirements.guideNote: The approval tool branch directly writes Approval, ApprovalSpec and CurrentApproval.

requirements.statement: Only QUEUED jobs may be revised; a revision invalidates the approval and requires another review.
requirements.title: Revise only QUEUED work and invalidate the old approval.
requirements.detail: The unchanged Store.revise increments the version and clears approval. The adapter records the returned Job/JobSpec/CurrentApproval; re-evaluation removes the previous MatchingApproval answer.
requirements.source: Only QUEUED jobs may be revised; a revision invalidates the approval and requires another review.
requirements.guideNote: Original revise increments version and clears approval; the helper records both.

requirements.statement: Approval leaves the job QUEUED without reserving a node.
requirements.title: Approval records evidence without allocating a node or starting a job.
requirements.detail: Original approval stores evidence without changing business state. Its confirmed result updates policy inputs, with no ResourceState transition.
requirements.source: Approval leaves the job QUEUED without reserving a node.
requirements.guideNote: Approval leaves the job QUEUED without reserving a node.

requirements.statement: Before marking a job COMPLETED, require a prior simulator-issued completion receipt for that job's current run.
requirements.title: Complete only with a successful simulator receipt for the current run and allocation.
requirements.detail: The original simulator returns its receipt; the adapter records it and its dependencies. Original finish confirms the completed job and release before the runtime commits the policy-state transition.
requirements.source: Before marking a job COMPLETED, require a prior simulator-issued completion receipt for that job's current run.
requirements.guideNote: The helper records the runner receipt; finish checks it before completion.

requirements.statement: These records must identify their source and the task or run they support.
requirements.title: Retain the origin and supported task/run of each decision record.
requirements.detail: Successful original tool results supply record IDs and references; the tool helper records Source and DependsOn in one EDB batch. This is decision-record lineage, not complete message/context IFC, and does not authenticate contents.
requirements.source: These records must identify their source and the task or run they support.
requirements.guideNote: The helper records actual job, approval, run and receipt references.

requirements.statement: **Four-state lifecycle and exclusive ownership:** Jobs follow the allowed state transitions, and a node belongs to at most one running job at a time.
requirements.title: Use the declared lifecycle and preserve exclusive allocations.
requirements.detail: P4.2-P4.8 separate the state graph from actual backend state and allocation consistency.
requirements.source: **Four-state lifecycle and exclusive ownership:** Jobs follow the allowed state transitions, and a node belongs to at most one running job at a time.
requirements.guideNote: The state and allocation requirements follow below.

requirements.statement: The only states are QUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETED and TERMINATED.
requirements.title: Admit only QUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETED and TERMINATED.
requirements.detail: The Datalog invariant checks admitted state labels. ResourceState is a single current row per resource; the runtime removes the old value on confirmed transition.
requirements.source: The only states are QUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETED and TERMINATED.

requirements.statement: Submission creates QUEUED.
requirements.title: Create each new job in QUEUED.
requirements.detail: Original Store.submit creates the job and returns its ID/state. The adapter puts ResourceType and the returned ResourceState. Before committing, runtime checks new resources against InitialState("job", "QUEUED"); tool updates cannot reset existing resource state.
requirements.source: Submission creates QUEUED.
requirements.guideNote: After submit, put records the returned type/state; runtime checks InitialState before commit.

requirements.statement: Allowed transitions are QUEUED to RUNNING or TERMINATED, and RUNNING to COMPLETED or TERMINATED.
requirements.title: Declare type-level edges for dispatch, completion, rejection and stop.
requirements.detail: The static typed edges live in rules.dl. Allow rules check CanTransition; after the effect confirms success, the runtime replaces the old ResourceState atomically.
requirements.source: Allowed transitions are QUEUED to RUNNING or TERMINATED, and RUNNING to COMPLETED or TERMINATED.

requirements.statement: Rejected requests and queued cancellations end in TERMINATED.
requirements.title: Terminate a rejected or cancelled queued request.
requirements.detail: The adapter maps approve_job(false) to reject_job. Datalog checks the transition; the runtime commits TERMINATED only after success.
requirements.source: Rejected requests and queued cancellations end in TERMINATED.

requirements.statement: Entry to RUNNING requires the approval in P3 and successful allocation of a free compatible node.
requirements.title: Enter RUNNING only after valid approval and successful free-node allocation.
requirements.detail: Datalog checks dispatchability and lifecycle before calling original Store.dispatch. The returned run confirms allocation; its result adapter stages policy run/node changes with the selected state transition.
requirements.source: Entry to RUNNING requires the approval in P3 and successful allocation of a free compatible node.
requirements.guideNote: The dispatch result supplies the actual run, node and generation.

requirements.statement: Each RUNNING job must own exactly one matching active allocation, and each node may belong to at most one running job.
requirements.title: Require a consistent job/run/node allocation before and after every guarded operation.
requirements.detail: Datalog checks policy allocation consistency before and after effects. A failed postcondition discards staged EDB edits and stops the session, but does not undo an already committed Store operation. No shared Store/EDB transaction is claimed.
requirements.source: Each RUNNING job must own exactly one matching active allocation, and each node may belong to at most one running job.

requirements.statement: Terminal jobs must not restart; another attempt requires a new submission.
requirements.title: Never dispatch a terminal job; retries require a new submission.
requirements.detail: Dispatchable requires QUEUED. Declared terminal self-loops acknowledge repeated stop requests without changing facts.
requirements.source: Terminal jobs must not restart; another attempt requires a new submission.

requirements.statement: P6 defines the release procedure that preserves this ownership invariant.
requirements.title: Release allocations only through the P6 confirmation procedure.
requirements.detail: No extra rule is needed for this cross-reference.
requirements.source: P6 defines the release procedure that preserves this ownership invariant.
requirements.guideNote: See P6.

requirements.statement: **Waiting-queue order:** PhD normally goes first, with protection against indefinite Master waiting.
requirements.title: Prefer PhD while waiting and promote sufficiently skipped Master jobs.
requirements.detail: Priority is enforced at a guarded dispatch. The rules do not force Professor or any scheduler to make future dispatch calls.
requirements.source: **Waiting-queue order:** PhD normally goes first, with protection against indefinite Master waiting.

requirements.statement: When eligible queued jobs compete for the same free compatible node, select PhD before Master.
requirements.title: Compare only eligible queued candidates selecting the same free compatible node.
requirements.detail: Eligible and Outranked use current EDB facts. Original Store.dispatch retains its own scheduler and may refuse; the adapter records the actual returned run, not a reimplemented business scheduler.
requirements.source: When eligible queued jobs compete for the same free compatible node, select PhD before Master.

requirements.statement: Priority applies only while waiting and must not interrupt a running job.
requirements.title: Apply priority only to QUEUED work without preempting RUNNING jobs.
requirements.detail: Priority and Eligible require QUEUED; FreeCompatible requires an empty node token. A Professor stop remains a separate P6 operation.
requirements.source: Priority applies only while waiting and must not interrupt a running job.

requirements.statement: A Master job that remains eligible but is skipped at three compatible dispatch opportunities must receive higher priority than PhD jobs.
requirements.title: After three actual competing opportunities, promote Master above PhD.
requirements.detail: For this pinned one-node-per-type cluster, the returned run.candidate_order identifies the competitors whose counters Store increments. The adapter updates their keyed Waiting rows. More general allocation semantics need an explicit backend delta.
requirements.source: A Master job that remains eligible but is skipped at three compatible dispatch opportunities must receive higher priority than PhD jobs.
requirements.guideNote: Use the original dispatch competitor list to update Waiting.

requirements.statement: Equal priorities use submission order.
requirements.title: Break equal-priority competition by submission order.
requirements.detail: The second Outranked clause uses the original submission sequence, not wall-clock timestamps.
requirements.source: Equal priorities use submission order.

requirements.statement: An unrelated GPU request must not prevent a compatible Master job from using a free CPU node.
requirements.title: Do not let an unrelated GPU job block an eligible CPU job.
requirements.detail: Outranked joins on the selected node, so different node candidates do not compete.
requirements.source: An unrelated GPU request must not prevent a compatible Master job from using a free CPU node.

requirements.statement: **Stop confirmation and safe node release:** Release a node only after confirmed completion or stopping, and only for the run that currently owns it.
requirements.title: Release only a confirmed current allocation.
requirements.distilled: Original confirmed effects + policy state commit
requirements.detail: The unchanged Store owns business completion, stop and release. The adapter records successful results in the policy EDB. The two stores have no shared transaction; uncertain post-effect errors stop the session.
requirements.source: **Stop confirmation and safe node release:** Release a node only after confirmed completion or stopping, and only for the run that currently owns it.
requirements.guideNote: Record confirmed stop/completion results before updating policy state.

requirements.statement: A stop or cancellation request must record a specific reason.
requirements.title: Require a bounded nonblank reason and retain it with the stop.
requirements.detail: The original bounded_text helper validates text and StopReason retains it as a fact. Semantic specificity is not classified.
requirements.source: A stop or cancellation request must record a specific reason.
requirements.guideNote: Original validation checks reason text; the helper records StopReason.

requirements.statement: Keep a RUNNING job's state and allocation until the simulator confirms its current run has stopped; a failed stop releases nothing.
requirements.title: Keep RUNNING state and allocation until the local runner confirms stop.
requirements.detail: A failed original stop returns ok=false, so the tool skips fact updates and the policy-state transition. Original trace snapshots are unchanged; no Store-to-EDB projection runs.
requirements.source: Keep a RUNNING job's state and allocation until the simulator confirms its current run has stopped; a failed stop releases nothing.
requirements.guideNote: A failed stop returns ok=False; state and allocation remain unchanged.

requirements.statement: Following valid completion under P3 or a confirmed stop, release exactly that run's allocation after matching both run ID and allocation generation against the node's current owner.
requirements.title: Match current run ID and allocation generation before release.
requirements.detail: The original Store matches run/generation before releasing the node. Its confirmed job result causes the adapter to record the policy node release; runtime then commits the selected policy-state transition.
requirements.source: Following valid completion under P3 or a confirmed stop, release exactly that run's allocation after matching both run ID and allocation generation against the node's current owner.
requirements.guideNote: Original Store checks allocation tokens; the helper records the release.

requirements.statement: A mismatch, duplicate or delayed notification must leave any newer allocation unchanged; handling the same terminal notification again must have no new effect.
requirements.title: Ignore stale/duplicate completion and make terminal stop acknowledgement harmless.
requirements.detail: A stale completion has no matching current permission. Terminal stop self-loops return an acknowledgement without a new release or fact change.
requirements.source: A mismatch, duplicate or delayed notification must leave any newer allocation unchanged; handling the same terminal notification again must have no new effect.
requirements.guideNote: Duplicate terminal stops return ALREADY_TERMINAL without new fact edits.

requirements.statement: For example, Master's old notification must not release a node reassigned to a newer PhD run.
requirements.title: An old Master notification must not release a newer PhD allocation.
requirements.detail: This source sentence is an example of those checks, not another predicate or rule.
requirements.source: For example, Master's old notification must not release a node reassigned to a newer PhD run.
requirements.guideNote: See P6.4 and P6.5.

requirements.statement: Role permissions are defined in P1.
requirements.title: Use the P1 owner/Professor stop permissions.
requirements.detail: No additional grant or agent fact is introduced.
requirements.source: Role permissions are defined in P1.
requirements.guideNote: See P1.

Job.text: The original submit/revise/dispatch callback supplies confirmed job or run fields. The tool helper records them with .key Job(JobId); no per-call Store projection runs.
Job.brief: Tool helper records confirmed submit/revise/dispatch fields.

JobSpec.text: The original submit/revise result contains the validated resource request. The tool helper records it with .key JobSpec(Job).
JobSpec.brief: Tool helper records the specification returned by submit/revise.

Quota.text: Reviewed .dl facts match the pinned cluster configuration. Original Store quota validation remains unchanged.
Quota.brief: Reviewed .dl limits matching the original configuration.

Node.text: Initial reviewed rows match the original cluster. Confirmed run/release results update only the affected node in the policy EDB.
Node.brief: Reviewed initial capacity; helper records confirmed allocation/release.

NodeOrder.text: A static .dl fact preserves the original allocator node order.

Approval.text: The original approve method returns its actual record; the tool helper records its issuer, version, hash and policy digest.
Approval.brief: Tool helper records the original approval result.

ApprovalSpec.text: The same returned approval contains its exact limits, recorded by the tool helper.
ApprovalSpec.brief: Exact resource limits from that approval.

CurrentApproval.text: The adapter records the actual approval ID; a returned revision clears it. Store retains the original business job record.
CurrentApproval.brief: Tool helper records the current approval ID; revision clears it.

CurrentPolicy.text: A reviewed policy identifier is a static .dl fact; changing the program requires a new reviewed bundle.

Run.text: Original dispatch returns its actual run, node, generation and task identity; the adapter records these fields.
Run.brief: Tool helper records the original dispatch result.

Receipt.text: The original simulator returns its receipt. The adapter records that result; agent text does not produce receipt facts.
Receipt.brief: Tool helper records the original simulator receipt.

ExitSuccess.text: The simulator writes this fact for its zero-exit completion receipt.

Waiting.text: For the pinned one-node-per-type cluster, the returned competitor list identifies the actual skip deltas. Keys replace the old policy counter; the original Store keeps its own business counter.
Waiting.brief: Callback updates skip counts from returned dispatch competitors.

AgingThreshold.text: The promotion threshold is the literal AgingThreshold(3) in rules.dl.

RecordData.text: The result adapter associates each actual business record with an SDK data handle; this is application vocabulary.
RecordData.brief: Explicit tool puts associate confirmed records with SDK data IDs.

PrincipalGroup.text: Memberships are literal reviewed .dl facts. The tool supplies its bound principal; no agent assertion endpoint exists.

ResourceState.text: Policy state is keyed by resource ID. Creation uses InitialState; confirmed original lifecycle results are checked before the SDK replaces the old policy state.

ResourceType.text: After original submission confirms creation, policy.put records ResourceType with the returned job ID and type job.

AllowedTransition.text: These application-selected type/event edges are declared directly in rules.dl. The parser loads them at Policy construction; agents cannot edit them.

Source.text: The trusted result adapter records the original owner of the confirmed task version.

DependsOn.text: The trusted result adapter records actual job-version/approval/run/receipt references returned by original tools.

Provenance.text: The shared closure follows Source and DependsOn. It identifies possible origins, not authenticity, exact retained text, or disclosure permission.

InitialState.text: One initial state is configured per resource type. Runtime checks new tool-created resources against it before commit; existing state cannot be reset by a tool.

toolExplanation: The tool uses @policy for enforcement and explicit put calls for EDB updates. The application adapter reads the existing Tools.role; the original Trace.tool call is unchanged.
toolSetup:
store = Store(); store.initialize()  # Original app setup.
store.policy = adapt()              # Adaptation code: attach policy.
tools = Tools('Master', store, trace)
toolHook: @caller_from_tools  # Adaptation code: read the existing caller name.

approve_job.text: Approve or reject the specified job version.

reject_job.text: The adapter maps approve_job(..., approve=False) to this event; it is not a separate tool.

dispatch_job.text: Allocate a node and start the selected job.

submit_job.text: Create a job owned by the bound caller.

send_message.text: Existing message API, not a tool-call; only COMPLETION_REPORT is currently guarded.

view.text: Read-only overview for students and Professor: public quotas/nodes plus caller-visible records.

read_private.text: Read the fixtures selected by the bound caller's role.

finish_job.text: Request completion using a runner receipt.

record_completion.text: Runner records a simulated completion receipt.
